settings.title: Settings
settings.workspaces.title: {{count}} workspace
settings.workspaces.none: A workspace exists once a repository is registered in it. Repositories says how one joins.
settings.list.browser: A machine's own settings are on the desktop, where the machine is.
settings.theme.label: Theme
settings.theme.hint: System follows the computer's own light or dark setting.
settings.language.label: Language
settings.language.hint: The window's own words, and Daoris's lines on a session's record. What agents, people and the service write is shown as written.
settings.home.label: Daoris home
settings.home.hint: The Daoris home. Every file on this page lives under it, and a terminal's daoris reads the same folder; nothing of Daoris's lives under your profile.
settings.home.hintOverridden: The Daoris home. Every file on this page lives under it; nothing of Daoris's lives under your profile. The line below says which folder a terminal's daoris reads.
settings.home.hintThisStart: The Daoris home, named for this start alone. Every file on this page lives under it; nothing of Daoris's lives under your profile. A terminal's daoris does not read this folder: it reads the one DAORIS_HOME names for your account, if it names one.
settings.notify.body: Nobody should have to watch a driver. This machine can say so when a session stops to ask you something, or ends without you asking — never for an ending you caused, because a notice about what you just pressed is one you learn to dismiss unread.
settings.notify.label: Notify me when a session parks
settings.notify.terminal: Also `daoris driver notify on|off` — one file, either door; a machine with no screen says it on its console.
settings.notify.on: This machine will tell you when a session needs you.
settings.notify.off: This machine will not interrupt you. The records still say everything they said.
settings.strikes.body: A session that fails leaves its quest open and untouched, so the driver's next look considers it again — which is right when the failure was a passing one, and expensive when it was not. Measured: one quest whose session could not start ran eighteen times, and every run spent an account.
settings.cooloff.label: Cool-off when no time is named
settings.cooloff.terminal: Also `daoris driver cooloff <minutes>` — one file, either door.
settings.cooloff.body: When an agent refuses a turn for its account's limit and names no time it resets, the account cools this many minutes before Daoris starts on it again. Long enough that a spent account is not started on at every look; short enough that a wrong guess costs an hour, not an evening. A limit that names its reset cools until then.
settings.cooloff.set: An account whose agent names no reset now cools {{count}} minute.
settings.cooloff.set_other: An account whose agent names no reset now cools {{count}} minutes.
settings.strikes.label: Failures before a quest parks
settings.strikes.set: A quest is parked after {{count}} failed session, and waits for you.
settings.strikes.set_other: A quest is parked after {{count}} failed sessions, and waits for you.
settings.strikes.never: This machine never parks a quest.
settings.strikes.zero: Zero means it keeps trying. A quest that fails for a reason no retry can fix will be started again on every look the driver takes, and every start spends a real account.
settings.strikes.terminal: Also `daoris driver strikes <n>`; `daoris driver retry <quest>` starts a parked one again. Stand-downs, declines, stops and held repositories never count.
